title: Pilot: The Showrunner cut (tiger, roach)
_note: research/39 pilot. Same facts as originals-01 tiger + roach. Persona: deadpan nature narrator who is a meatball and takes every mention of eating personally. Fork = silent running gag, tink = the one sting.

beats.say: If you shave a tiger, it's still striped.
beats.quiz:
SHAVE A TIGER,
IT'S STILL
STRIPED
beats.bonus: No two tigers have the same stripe pattern.
beats.short_title: Is a Tiger's Skin Striped Too? 🐯
beats.loop_say: I'm not saying you should try it. I'm just saying,

beats.say: True. The stripes aren't just on the fur. The skin underneath is striped too.
And every tiger's pattern is different, like a fingerprint. So if one eats you, you'll know exactly who did it.
Stripes, all the way down. As a meatball, I relate. Unfortunately.
A cockroach can live for a week without its head.
beats.quiz:
A COCKROACH CAN
LIVE A WEEK
WITHOUT ITS HEAD
beats.bonus: Cockroaches can hold their breath for around forty minutes.
beats.short_title: Can a Cockroach Really Live Without Its Head? 🪳
beats.loop_say: And people call me the gross one. Meanwhile,

beats.say: True. Cockroaches breathe through tiny holes along their body, not through their head. So the head was basically optional.
Without a mouth, it can't drink. So after about a week, it dies of thirst. Meanwhile, I lose one bite, and they call it dinner.
Headless. Still fine. Honestly, the most confident thing I have ever met.
